tips.text: Hold every copy and fuse into your highest roll last; fusing low rolls into low rolls wastes copies.
Put Oull in the first slot whenever you have one; it counts as a hit, so you earn Murmurs without ranking the Lich up.
Clear every enemy before you extract; Thralls spawn on a timer and on kills, up to 10 per mission.
Hold your stabs until one Requiem is revealed, then stab only to test something new.
Bring a wide nuke frame such as Saryn, Volt, Mirage or Rhino so you hit the Larvling kill count in time.
Run long missions like Survival, Defense or Interception for Murmurs, then short Exterminate or Capture runs once you only need Lich spawns.
When your Lich shows up with nothing to test, leave it alone so it converts up to 10 more Thralls, then down it three times and it leaves.
Stock one or two of each Requiem mod before you Mercy a Larvling so a missing mod never stalls the hunt.
Run the Murmur phase in public squads; other players' failed stabs fill your Murmurs too, but only when they actually stab.
Use your Requiem Ultimatum solo; in a squad it can spawn a teammate's Lich instead.
Run the Saturn Proxima fight solo in a Railjack that can survive; grouping adds no reward.
Farm Larvlings on a Cassini Capture; if it stops spawning them, switch to any level 20 or higher Grineer Exterminate.
Mercy with the Warframe whose element you want on the weapon; Toxin, Electricity and Heat frames are the common picks.
Finish the mission for every wrong Larvling, and never take a consolation weapon; taking any Larvling clears your reject list.
Once one Requiem is known, stab on every spawn for the Murmur chunk, as long as you can handle the higher-level Lich nodes.
Mercy every Thrall on an Interception before it hits 100 percent; the end of the mission clears them.
Drop invisibility before the flash; it can stop a Larvling spawning.
The Zarr is past its prime; most players farm it for mastery or On-Call crew use.
Expect one to two hours per Lich once you have a rhythm, and three to five Liches for a 60 percent roll.
